issue.title: Fix potential race condition in distributed mode leading to duplicated tasks
issue.body:
## Description
In some circumstances like a network partitioning, some tasks might
be duplicated. Sometimes, this lead to a race condition where a lost
task overwrites the result of the last successful task in the backend.

In order to avoid this race condition we prevent updating the result if
it's already in successful state.

This fix has been done for KV backends only and therefore won't work
with other backends.

Hello, I had this error also. 

The workaround I found is to deactivate the restore_at_shutdown : 
`kombu.transport.redis.QoS.restore_at_shutdown = False`

That doesn't correct the problème in which a gevent worker does not change the Status of the message when it is shutdown, but that prevent the risk to have task executed twice.

Hi @auvipy, I think a have a test case for this problem.

I'm running celery with gevent pool with the next env and I have the same problem:
```
rabbitmq          3.8.12
----
python packages:
gevent            21.1.2
amqp              5.0.5
kombu             5.0.2
celery            5.0.5
```

# Expected Behavior
Ack was sent for any task that completed after warm shutdown.

# Actual Behavior
I have running background task with `acks_late=True`.
When I press `ctrl-c` worker waiting for the pool to the last task.
Then task successfully executes worker continue the shutdown process but ack for the tasks wasn't send.
After consumer disconnection rabbitmq returns a message without ack back to a queue.


I think the main reason for this problem is that after warm shutdown a consumer can't send ack for completed tasks because the `synloop` isn't running already. Gevent task just append promises to `Consumer._pending_operations` but `Consumer.perform_pending_operations` isn't called in shutdown process.

Currently, I fixed the problem by adding an extra bootstep on the consumer shutdown process:
```python
class FixAck(bootsteps.StartStopStep):
    requires = {
        "celery.worker.consumer.connection:Connection",
    }

    def shutdown(self, c):
        c.perform_pending_operations()
        
app.steps["consumer"].add(FixAck)
```


# Steps to Reproduce

I added two prints to debug the problem:
* `celery.worker.request.Request.acknowledge` - `REQUEST ACK` to see when a task request call ack
* `kombu.message.Message.ack` - `KOMBU ACK` to see when an actual ack was called

Minimal example to reproduce the problem:
```python
from time import sleep

from celery import Celery
from gevent import getcurrent

app = Celery("tasks", broker="amqp://guest:guest@localhost:15672//")
app.conf.update(
    result_backend="redis",
    result_persistent=True,
    result_expires=3600 * 2,
    redis_host="localhost",
    redis_port="16379",
    redis_db="7",
    redis_password="",
)


@app.task(acks_late=True)
def add(x, y):
    print(f"ID {id(getcurrent())}")
    sleep(10)
    return x + y
```

### Other Dependencies

N/A

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

Let's assume I have this task: ```python @shared_task(acks_late=True) def printer(i, sleep_amount): sleep(sleep_amount) print(i) ``` I'm running it as 2 chains from `shell_plus` with the following commands: ```python In [2]: from celery import chain In [3]: chain1 = chain(*[printer.si(i, 10) for i in range(5)]) In [4]: chain2 = chain(*[printer.si(i, 20) for i in range(5, 10)]) In [5]: chain1(); chain2() Out[5]: ``` The worker picks up the tasks and runs both chains fine. At some point, I initiate a warm shutdown. Just as the task with the shorter amount of sleep finishes I initiate a cold shutdown. Therefore, a task from `chain1` managed to finish (printing 2) while the task from `chain2` (printing 6) didn't manage to finish. Here's the output for that: ```python Using settings.DEBUG leads to a memory leak, never use this setting in production environments! [2021-11-16 06:50:32,587: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-1] 0 [2021-11-16 06:50:32,588: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-1] [2021-11-16 06:50:32,628: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-1] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[c275e1b9-3017-4fa3-a584-dee791172a26] succeeded in 10.08305716200266s: None [2021-11-16 06:50:42,601: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-4] 5 [2021-11-16 06:50:42,603: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-4] [2021-11-16 06:50:42,646: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-4] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[66da0ef9-d2bc-41cb-8d83-6234be404e4e] succeeded in 20.09970868000164s: None [2021-11-16 06:50:42,661: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-2] 1 [2021-11-16 06:50:42,661: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-2] [2021-11-16 06:50:42,692: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-2] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[69d31adf-62bd-47ab-a4a7-387d9e9a3cd9] succeeded in 10.062553351999668s: None ^C worker: Hitting Ctrl+C again will terminate all running tasks! worker: Warm shutdown (MainProcess) [2021-11-16 06:50:52,694: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-4] 2 [2021-11-16 06:50:52,695: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-4] [2021-11-16 06:50:52,708: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-4] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[7a76ce38-d1a5-4dd6-b615-482fcd04f971] succeeded in 10.041315492999274s: None ^C worker: Cold shutdown (MainProcess) ``` After the cold shutdown is done, I decided to restart my worker. Let's take a look at the output: ```python Using settings.DEBUG leads to a memory leak, never use this setting in production environments! [2021-11-16 06:51:32,853: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-4] 2 [2021-11-16 06:51:32,853: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-2] 3 [2021-11-16 06:51:32,855: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-2] [2021-11-16 06:51:32,855: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-4] [2021-11-16 06:51:32,896: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-2] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[73863b0c-9795-448a-a14f-69065811649d] succeeded in 10.075809672001924s: None [2021-11-16 06:51:32,900: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-4] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[7a76ce38-d1a5-4dd6-b615-482fcd04f971] succeeded in 10.079479289001029s: None [2021-11-16 06:51:42,864: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-1] 6 [2021-11-16 06:51:42,865: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-1] [2021-11-16 06:51:42,901: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-1] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[58ef65ce-8e2d-46bf-8b0b-af86931f72b6] succeeded in 20.080117989000428s: None [2021-11-16 06:51:42,917: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-4] 3 [2021-11-16 06:51:42,917: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-4] [2021-11-16 06:51:42,922: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-4] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[73863b0c-9795-448a-a14f-69065811649d] succeeded in 10.019568042000174s: None [2021-11-16 06:51:42,929: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-3] 4 [2021-11-16 06:51:42,929: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-3] [2021-11-16 06:51:42,936: INFO/ForkPoolWorker-3] Task listmatch.tasks.printer[eafe6809-81f2-4044-ba27-c85d0a3d4692] succeeded in 10.04345621900211s: None ^C worker: Hitting Ctrl+C again will terminate all running tasks! worker: Warm shutdown (MainProcess) ^C worker: Cold shutdown (MainProcess) ``` We can see that 2 is printed again. This is the task that managed to finish during the warm shutdown and it makes no sense to repeat that task. 3 is also printed as soon as 2 which suggests that the tasks for 2 and 3 were executed in parallel. Furthermore, the repeated 2 will continue to a repeated 3 while the normal 3 will continue to normal 4. When we restarted we basically went into executing 3 chains. Checking `celery inspect active` during task execution will show 3 tasks being handled at a time, this was not true before the warm/cold shutdown combo: ``` -> celery@e8a31ea31f8f: OK * {'id': '58ef65ce-8e2d-46bf-8b0b-af86931f72b6', 'name': 'listmatch.tasks.printer', 'args': (6, 20), 'kwargs': {}, 'type': 'listmatch.tasks.printer', 'hostname': 'celery@e8a31ea31f8f', 'time_start': 1637074282.8212085, 'acknowledged': False, 'delivery_info': {'exchange': '', 'routing_key': 'celery', 'priority': 0, 'redelivered': True}, 'worker_pid': 1380} * {'id': '7a76ce38-d1a5-4dd6-b615-482fcd04f971', 'name': 'listmatch.tasks.printer', 'args': (2, 10), 'kwargs': {}, 'type': 'listmatch.tasks.printer', 'hostname': 'celery@e8a31ea31f8f', 'time_start': 1637074282.8203754, 'acknowledged': False, 'delivery_info': {'exchange': '', 'routing_key': 'celery', 'priority': 0, 'redelivered': True}, 'worker_pid': 1399} * {'id': '73863b0c-9795-448a-a14f-69065811649d', 'name': 'listmatch.tasks.printer', 'args': (3, 10), 'kwargs': {}, 'type': 'listmatch.tasks.printer', 'hostname': 'celery@e8a31ea31f8f', 'time_start': 1637074282.8203804, 'acknowledged': False, 'delivery_info': {'exchange': '', 'routing_key': 'celery', 'priority': 0, 'redelivered': False}, 'worker_pid': 1388} 1 node online. ``` It seems to me that tasks from chains that manage to finish during warm shutdowns that are followed by cold shutdowns don't get acknowledged, therefore they return to the queue + the next task they queued because they're a part of a chain. Therefore you get another chain.

# Expected Behavior Any task that manages to finish (with or without an error) during warm shutdowns should get acknowledged if `acks_late=True`. # Actual Behavior As described in the minimal test case, if a task from a chain finishes during a warm shutdown followed by a cold shutdown it won't get acknowledged. It will return to the queue + the next task from the chain will be in the queue as well.
